info.name: Galana Fuel Card Partner API
info.description:
jpl_fuel_card partner API (/api/method/jpl_fuel_card.api.partner.v1.*).

Set base_url (environment or collection variable) to your Frappe site, e.g. http://localhost:8000 or https://erpstaging.jaguar-petroleum.com.

1. Run a Login request in Auth — it saves the access/refresh token for that role automatically.
2. Each folder already points its Authorization at the right saved token (galana_access_token / jaguar_access_token / pos_access_token).
3. For Transaction Events, set the client_id and client_secret collection variables from your OAuth Client record first — the request signs itself.
4. Portal endpoints (Galana Portal folder) take an 'actor' parameter — the real Galana portal user's email, not the service account. The collection variables admin_email / finance_maker_email / finance_checker_email / ops_email / station_manager_email / auditor_email are pre-filled with the local crm site's real users (as of 2026-10-07), already wired into the requests that semantically need that role — e.g. Create Top-up uses finance_maker_email, Decide Top-up uses finance_checker_email. These are only emails, not secrets; their passwords are not in this collection.
5. Most request bodies/params are pre-filled with real example values from the local crm site (station TEST-ST-01, vehicle KTEST 001, dealer 'TEST Dealer', POS device TEST-POS-0002, a real completed transaction g3ie40lg7o, etc.) so you can mostly just hit Send. A few genuinely dynamic values chain automatically between requests: POS > Authorise saves last_ticket_reference/last_authorization_code (used by Start Fuelling, Cancel Transaction, Jaguar > Transaction Events); Create Top-up/Adjustment/Reversal each save their own id (used by the matching Decide request). Run the 'Create'/'Authorise' request before the one that depends on it.

item.name: Jaguar (Brian)

request.description: Is there enough float for this amount? Prepaid returns float_balance; credit returns credit_limit/utilized_credit/available_credit.
Current EPRA price per litre. Omit product for all products.

Push one completed POS transaction. Requires X-Client-Id/X-Timestamp/X-Signature — computed automatically by this request's pre-request script. Set collection variables client_id and client_secret first (from your OAuth Client record). ticketReference/authorizationCode default to whatever the POS folder's Authorise request last saved — run that first, or paste in a real Reserved ticket. transactionNumber uses Postman's {{$timestamp}} so repeat sends don't just return 'duplicate': true. Idempotent on ptsId+transactionNumber.

exec: // Fill in collection variables client_id / client_secret from your OAuth Client record first.
console.warn("Set client_id and client_secret collection variables before calling transaction_events.");

item.description: The three endpoints available to Jaguar (require_partner_user: Galana, Jaguar or POS).

item.name: POS

request.description: Device must be Active, allocated to a station, and running approved software.
Read-only check — does not consume the ticket. Defaults to whatever Authorise last saved; swap for ticket_reference if you prefer.
Status of a ticket: Reserved, Dispensing, Consumed, Expired, Refunded, Pending Reconciliation.

Reserve fuel for a vehicle. Returns the 8-digit authorisation code and expiry. Refused if float is insufficient — top up the wallet first (Wallet folder) if customer_float shows a negative balance. On success, saves last_ticket_reference / last_authorization_code for the rest of this folder and for Jaguar > Transaction Events.

exec: console.warn("ticket_reference not found in response:", body);
console.warn("authorization_code not found in response:", body);

request.description: Moves a Reserved ticket to Dispensing. Run Authorise first — this uses whatever it last saved.
Only a Reserved ticket can be cancelled — don't run this after Start Fuelling in the same chain, it'll correctly fail once the ticket is Dispensing.
Send a fuelling OTP to the driver's phone. id_number is the driver's national ID as recorded on the Fuel Card Driver record.
Confirm a single-use, expiring OTP. otp is a placeholder — use the real code sent by Request OTP.

item.name: Galana Portal (service account only)

request.description: Customers Galana serves (Galana Settings.galana_customers).
g3ie40lg7o is the real TEST-TX-0030 fuelling record on the local crm site — swap for any id from Transactions (list).
Updates the real TEST-ST-01 fixture (safe, it's test data). Clear station_id to create a new station instead — then data needs station_name, dealer, region, county at minimum.
status: ACTIVE, SUSPENDED or DEACTIVATED.
device_id TEST-POS-0099 is new, won't collide with the existing TEST-POS-0001/2/3.
TEST-1.0 already exists (used by the POS folder's examples) — TEST-2.0 is new, won't collide.

Left blank deliberately: run Approved POS Software Versions above and copy a row name in. Do NOT remove TEST-1.0's row unless you don't need the POS folder's examples (pos_device, authorise, etc.) to keep working — they all assume software_version TEST-1.0 is approved.

Closes the previous price the day before effective_from. Refuses back-dated prices — effective_from must be after the current price's effective_from (2026-10-06 on the local site), so this uses a December date. epra-prices:manage belongs to OPS_FUEL_CARD (and SYSTEM_ADMIN).
Makers see only their own; checkers/admin/auditor see all.
Requires FINANCE_MAKER or SYSTEM_ADMIN actor. Saves the new request's id to last_topup_id for Decide Top-up below.

exec: console.warn("top-up id not found in response:", body);

request.description: Requires FINANCE_CHECKER or SYSTEM_ADMIN actor, and cannot be the maker — that's why this uses finance_checker_email, not finance_maker_email. decision: Approved or Rejected (comment required for Rejected).
direction: Credit or Debit. Saves the new request's id to last_adjustment_id for Decide Adjustment below.

exec: console.warn("adjustment id not found in response:", body);

request.description: transaction is a completed (Successful Fueling) Fuel Card Transaction Log name — g3ie40lg7o is the real TEST-TX-0030 fixture on the local site. One open reversal per fuelling, so this only works once per transaction; swap for a different completed transaction id if you get 'already has an open reversal'. OPS_FUEL_CARD, FINANCE_MAKER or SYSTEM_ADMIN may request. Saves the new request's id to last_reversal_id for Decide Reversal below.

exec: console.warn("reversal id not found in response:", body);

request.description: g3ie40lg7o is the real TEST-TX-0030 fixture — a settlement's id is the completed fuelling's own Fuel Card Transaction Log name.
credit_note_id is '<settlement id>:<UNDER_CANOPY|CONTRACTUAL>'. Discount rates are currently 0 on the local site, so the amount will show 0 — the lookup still succeeds either way.

Checks a portal user's password and returns their Galana roles. Used by the Next.js app's own login form. usr here is the user LOGGING IN, not an 'actor'. pwd is deliberately blank — it's a real account password, paste the actual one in yourself (never commit it).
Status and roles for one portal user — checked on every session.

role_names are the suffixes after 'Galana ', e.g. FINANCE_MAKER, SYSTEM_ADMIN. station_id only matters for STATION_DEALER_MANAGER. Requires users:manage (SYSTEM_ADMIN). email is a brand-new throwaway address, not a real account — the three requests below assume you ran this first and act on that same user, not on admin_email/finance_maker_email etc.
Any value other than 'ACTIVE' disables the account — INACTIVE is what a status read-back shows.
Sends Frappe's own password-reset email. No password is returned.

A FINANCE_MAKER/FINANCE_CHECKER actor may only change underCanopyDiscountPerL/jaguarDiscountPerL — enforced in the Next.js app, not here; this raw endpoint accepts whatever a SYSTEM_ADMIN actor sends. Try with finance_maker_email + only the two discount fields to mirror the app's own behaviour.
